_comment: Template for new users: copy it to hub.json and edit (the platform's bin/hubconf.py reads hub.json). Paths may start with ~; relative paths are relative to the hub root. Sections you don't need (assistant, alerts, backup, github…) can be deleted whole: the features that read them are simply off. Full explanation in README.md and docs/design/new-user.md.

owner._comment: You: address is the mailbox address letters to you are sent to (part of the protocol, don't change it); tag is your name as the owner label of the zh-Hant to-do lines (contracts/state-todo.v2.md; the English set labels you `owner`)

assistant._comment: Optional: a personal assistant (receives letters to the owner address, sends handoffs back). Without one, delete the whole section. Add "name" to call it by name in texts; unset, the UI language's generic term is used ("the personal assistant")

alerts._comment: Optional: alerts sent to Discord (bot token and channel id each in a file, not in version control). Without them, delete the whole section

_bus_dir_comment: The event bus (bus.db, hubbus.log). Deliberately outside the hub directory: sandboxed projects deny writes to ~/agent-hub/**, and a deny overrides the sandbox's allowWrite (tested in the 2026-10-22 pilot)

backup._comment: Optional: nightly encrypted backup (restic). The password is in .secrets/backup-password (keep another copy in your password manager), the B2 key in .secrets/b2-env. Without it, delete the whole section

github._comment: Optional: the account used to create GitHub repos when onboarding (gh auth login first)

ideas._comment: The maximum number of idea sandboxes (type: idea) at once, create-idea-sandbox.py / POST /v1/sandboxes

mailbox._comment: Project mailbox routing (bin/hubbus dispatch, docs/design/mailbox-routing.md): how many minutes to wait first when someone is using the project/the conversation partner is open, the context limit for continuing (beyond it a fresh one is dispatched), the maximum rounds handled per thread, the maximum dispatches per project per day

credentials._comment: User-level credential locations (policy.py → unreadable in every runtime's sandbox; blocked by the lease's --settings and the platform runner's profile too). dirs include everything below them, files are single files

capabilities._comment: The platform's list of capabilities (docs/design/capabilities.md): a project registry's enforce.capabilities accepts only names listed here, each capability with a profile fragment capabilities/<name>.sb. default_for: written into the registry automatically when that kind of project is created (create-idea-sandbox.py); risk: high ones are never added automatically, an agent-hub session changes the registry after the owner agrees

gpu.description: Run programs on the GPU (Metal), e.g. Blender renders. The file and network scope do not grow

cap_runner._comment: The platform runner (bin/cap-runner.py, bin/hub-run): job timeout default/maximum (seconds), the maximum running at once (always 1 per project)

runtime._comment: Which runtime the platform uses (a name in runtime_ports.RUNTIMES; docs/design/runtime-abstraction.md). Claude Code is just one implementation

lease._comment: Channel leases: anyone can host on these domains (including subdomains) and see who requests or what was posted, so WebFetch to them can only be approved one at a time, never "allowed for this whole lease" (the personal assistant's permission card reads the same list from the runner's GET /v1/policy)

hosts._comment: server: the ssh name of the machine that runs the hub, needed only when it runs on one machine and is driven from another; leave it empty when one machine does everything. mbp_home/mini_home: path translation for reading old transcripts, usually left empty

modules._comment: Features that can stay off (modules/<name>.yaml): adopted only when true. assistant needs the assistant section set up first, backup the backup section
